quote.text: It never ceases to amaze me: we all love ourselves more than other people, but care more about their opinion than our own. If a god appeared to us—or a wise human being, even—and prohibited us from concealing our thoughts or imagining anything without immediately shouting it out, we wouldn’t make it through a single day. That’s how much we value other people’s opinions—instead of our own.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that when we overvalue external validation, we risk shaping our children's sense of self around the fleeting opinions of others rather than the steadiness of inner conviction.
    • Model authenticity by nurturing in your children a respect for their own thoughts, teaching them that while advice can be valuable, their inner voice holds the wisdom of their true character.
  • Leadership
    • Embrace the importance of self-trust in leadership; when you prioritize your own judgments over the constant echo of external opinions, you lead with clarity and decisiveness.
    • Understand that genuine leadership means creating an environment where candid dialogue is encouraged—both from you and within your team—without falling prey to the need for universal approval.
  • Product Management
    • Apply the wisdom of valuing your own insights when making product decisions, ensuring that the vision for the product is driven by true value rather than the transient judgments of the market.
    • Balance stakeholder feedback with your strategic goals; let your inner compass guide innovation and improvement, fostering a product that reflects enduring principles over short-term trends.
